_about: One dated sentence at the top of each issue page (/issues/<topic>/), written from that page's own summary (tracked-issues.json or context.json) as of the date that data was checked. Update the sentence and its date together.

growth.text: council is rezoning Garibaldi Estates for more homes, and staff's draft budget proposes a full rewrite of the Official Community Plan starting in 2027.

housing_affordability.text: council has approved the land lease for 65 supportive homes at 39900 Government Road, BC Housing expects to start building in summer 2027, and a second building of affordable rentals has no funding yet.

homelessness.text: the District has closed the encampment behind Under One Roof for good, and the District and BC Housing are still choosing a site for the Province's temporary housing.

policing.text: Squamish is policed by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police under a contract, and the District pays most of the bill.

taxes_spending.text: staff's draft 2027 budget starts at a 10.4% property tax increase, about $342 for the average home, and the new council has not voted on it yet.

climate.text: the District's climate plan aims to cut the town's emissions at least 45% below 2010 levels by 2030 and be on track for net zero by 2050.

environment_lng.text: Woodfibre LNG is building its gas export plant, which council cannot stop, and its worker floatels run on a two year permit council approved in July 2025.

transportation.text: there is still no public bus from Squamish to Vancouver or Whistler, and in September 2026 local governments, the Lil'wat and Squamish Nations and the Province signed a memorandum to keep working on one.

parking.text: paid parking is a pilot at Darrell Bay only, running to the end of 2026, and staff report back in early 2027 on whether to expand it downtown.

economy.text: many Squamish residents commute out of town for work, and council's goal was a net increase in space for businesses by September 2026.

recreation_facilities.text: grant funded renovations at Brennan Park are nearly done, but a real expansion has no money set aside, and a task force is due to report options and costs around mid 2027.

flood_hazards_climate_resilience.text: a new $18 million sea dike at Xwu'nekw Park protects downtown, and borrowing for the 2026 flood upgrades still needs approval from voters before council can adopt it.

other_campaign_topics.text: child care in Squamish is scarce and expensive, and it is named as the main reason the local living wage is higher than Metro Vancouver's.
